name: Draft a changelog entry
description: Turn the commits since the last tag into a reviewed CHANGELOG.md entry.

repo_path.description: Absolute path to the git repository

version.description: Version label for the entry, e.g. 0.4.0

requirements.description: repo_path is a git repository with at least one commit
requirements.check: Run `git -C <repo_path> log -1 --oneline`; ok if it prints a commit

requirements.description: A file named .changelog-author in repo_path holds the preparer's name (used in the entry footer)
requirements.check: Run `cat <repo_path>/.changelog-author`; ok if it prints a non-empty name

collect.title: Collect commits
collect.instructions: List commits since the latest tag (all commits if there is no tag) with `git log --oneline`. Count them. Do not write anything yet.

range.description: The git range you used, e.g. v0.3.0..HEAD or HEAD

nothing_to_release.description: No commits since the last tag

draft.title: Write the entry
draft.instructions: Create CHANGELOG.md in repo_path (top heading `# Changelog`) or prepend to it a section `## <version>` with one bullet per user-visible change, grouped under Added / Changed / Fixed as appropriate. End the section with a line `Prepared by: <name from .changelog-author>`. Do not commit.

path.description: Absolute path to the file you wrote

bullets.description: Number of bullets in the new section (not lines in the file)

self_review.title: Check the entry against the commits
self_review.instructions: Re-read the commit list and the entry. Every commit must be represented or deliberately omitted (merge commits, chores). If anything is missing or wrong, go back and fix it.
